messages:
mohit_oncall: paging because we started seeing a burst of 5xx + gateway timeouts hitting the batcher around 12:02 UTC :rotating_light:
incident_bot: Incident created: HIGH - scheduler queue growth causing downstream gateway 504/502 spikes. Pager dispatched to @mohit_oncall and @sre_pager
mohit_oncall: seeing queue depth ~12k across scheduler shards, tail latency exploding. head-of-line blocking on shard-3
jamie_ops: confirmed client-side timeouts from gateway; replaying logs now. any customer-facing impact?
lucy_support: multiple customers reporting increased error rates in their dashboards. CS alerted enterprise accounts OOO impact window, working on comms
sandra_eng: logs show a hot partition in scheduler that isn't dispatching due to a KV lock on pending batches (kv-cache miss + lock contention). suspect runaway batching policy on recent rollout
kevin_runtime: rolled a lightweight change to batching thresholds yesterday, could be related. rolling that back asap if we can reproduce
mohit_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) stop new request routing to shard-3 2) enable emergency eviction on scheduler 3) reduce max-batch-size to 32 globally 4) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant
jamie_ops: executing step 1: updating routing policy to avoid shard-3 via dynamic route table (will take ~30s). ETA 30s
incident_bot: route update applied by jamie_ops at 12:05:21 UTC
lucy_support: CS: removing shard-3 should reduce immediate customer errors. sending note to affected customers: small blip, investigating
sandra_eng: step 2: enabling eviction. command:
```
# enable emergency eviction on all schedulers
curl -X POST https://infra.internal/scheduler/evict -d '{"mode":"aggressive"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```
kevin_runtime: started eviction, watching metric: scheduler.evictions.per_minute -> spike expected then drain
mohit_oncall: step 3: decreasing max-batch-size. applying config change to fleet now
jamie_ops: applied batch_size=32, propagation 45s
kevin_runtime: step 4: enabling fallback model variant for client-tier=free & tier=standard. Routing rule pushed
jamie_ops: gateway 504 count dropping by ~40% in the last 2m, p50 latency improving :thumbsup:
incident_bot: Alert: gateway.errors(5xx) decreased from 18% -> 6% over 5m window
sandra_eng: digging into root cause: the change to batching thresholds created long-lived pinned batches when tokenization latency varied per request, causing head-of-line where one large request blocked many small ones
mohit_oncall: long-term action items: revert threshold change, add canary with runtime flag, introduce per-request token bucket to avoid oversized batch blocking
lucy_support: CS update sent: we notified impacted customers and are monitoring. will provide post-mortem timeline in 24h
kevin_runtime: quick note: metric snapshot attached (link) - queue depth per-shard: shard-1 1.2k, shard-2 900, shard-3 drained to ~200 after routing removal
jamie_ops: handing off to @sandra_eng for deep-dive. I'm marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. on-call rotation: @sandra_eng will take lead for postmortem and followups
sandra_eng: ack taking lead. I'll coordinate with runtime and devex for the rollback and add an eval to catch regressing batching behavior
sre_pager: Thanks team. Please add any commands used to the incident runbook entry. If further paging happens I will escalate to infra-leads
mohit_oncall: final status: customer impact reduced to intermittent ~1-2% errors on small subset. mitigation successful for now. tracking rollback + e2e test as P0
jamie_ops: adding quick mitigation checklist to thread:
- isolate hot shard from routing
- enable eviction mode
- reduce max-batch-size
- route to fallback model variant
- notify CS + keep customers updated
sandra_eng: will schedule rollback to previous batching-thresholds in next maintenance window and add canary flags ASAP
lucy_support: noted, prepping customer follow-up with ETA and postmortem promise
incident_bot: Incident updated: MITIGATED -> MONITORING at 12:12:03 UTC
kevin_runtime: leaving a snippet for postmortem:
```
observed: sudden queue depth increase due to long-tail tokenization requests
root cause: batching threshold change created conditions for head-of-line blocking
mitigation: isolate shard, evict, reduce batch size, fallback route
remediation: revert change, add per-request guards, canary rollout
```
mohit_oncall: thanks all. reopening if error rate rises above 3% again. switching to monitoring channel for next 2h
jamie_ops: thx everyone — nice fast work on the live handoff and mitigations :clap:
